title: Business Development Brief
summary: Business development strategy informed by Notion data analysis and market positioning.
content:
Second Run Additions -- 2026-03-07

What the Notion Data Confirmed and Changed

Client Relationship Depth (ranked by content volume = trust = upsell potential)

1. Ambition Mechanical -- Deepest relationship

The dashboard has 20+ content items logged: published work, active shoots, idea backlog, strategy sessions. The "Working With Your Media Team" doc references "half a year of partnership -- and we're just getting started," and "over a year together" in the same document. This client has been with AOM the longest by far. The relationship is strong enough that Patrik and Ash's direct numbers are shared in the onboarding doc. Platform access is currently LinkedIn only -- that's a constraint worth noting and an upsell angle.

Content formats active for Ambition:

  • Project highlight reels (Refined Gardens, Fashion Square, Arrowhead INEOS, East Valley/West Valley, Civea)
  • Before/after progress videos
  • Instructional/educational videos (Chillers, Safety Videos, Orientation)
  • Recruitment/culture content (Lifeskills, Team Behind Us, Quality We Deliver)
  • Teasers and short-form
  • Drone footage (Civea, 8am Crane)
  • Instructional carousels (Adobe Suites Project)

The volume and variety here is significant. This isn't just "some videos" -- AOM is running a full content operation for this client. The $2k/month rate is even more clearly underpriced when you see how much is in flight.

2. ISA Industries -- Most complex scope

ISA has more distinct workstreams than any other client:

  • Brand video (hard deadline April 27, fully scripted with shot list)
  • Whitepaper/validation study video (separate deliverable, already has a narrative + edit structure doc)
  • Demo video (published)
  • Pitch deck photoshoot (published)
  • Episode 1 of a documentary series (in production, full production dashboard with story structure, interviews, shot list)
  • Marketing materials (idea backlog)

This is 4-5 distinct deliverables in various stages. The documentary series (ISA Ep. 1) is a 12-18 minute episode structured around three simultaneous storylines: technical breakthrough, funding, and independent validation. That's not a simple corporate video -- that's long-form documentary work at a level most agencies can't execute. AOM is doing this.

The relationship with Skylar (ISA co-founder) is the trust bridge. Skylar's music video and ISA's brand work are both AOM deliverables. That two-client-one-relationship dynamic is both a strength and a risk -- if the Skylar video goes poorly, it affects ISA. The first brief flagged this correctly.

3. KOHRS -- Active but earlier stage

Dashboard shows work from December 2025: Demo Day videos, Welcome to the Neighborhood, demolition footage shoots. The 12/5 strategy session notes logged a first meeting at Leigh's home -- this is a newer relationship. Content focus appears to be home renovation / remodeling (Inhabit Studio, product videos, demo day content). Status is in production for the December items. No clear indication this is still active vs. paused.

Important: KOHRS appears to be a design/renovation firm (references to "Inhabit Studio" and homeowner shoots). Not construction in the Ambition sense -- more residential design. Different vertical, different content needs.

4. LBX -- Documentary retainer, active

LBX has a 3-episode documentary series structure in production (Ep. 1 "The Risk", Ep. 2 "The Origin System", Ep. 3 "The Pillars"). All three episodes are marked "In Production" in the dashboard. There's an ElevenLabs audio file in the Ep. 2 folder -- suggesting AI voiceover is part of the production workflow for this client. The episode titles suggest LBX is a business/entrepreneurship brand, not a physical product company. The retainer proposal in their folder uses Slick City branding -- it was a template that wasn't fully updated. That's a process gap: proposals are being sent with wrong client branding.

5. Included Health -- One-off corporate video, significant scope

The Included Health deliverable is a $9,000 Scope of Work for 3-day event coverage (Client Summit). This is not a retainer -- it's a single high-value event shoot. Deliverables: summit hype reel, 10-15 interviews, full session recordings, all raw footage, camera LUTs. Workflow is Frame.io for review and delivery. Three-camera setup (Panasonic S5II, GH5, Ronin 4D).

This is AOM's highest-production-value documented scope. The professional workflow (Frame.io, redundant audio capture, three cameras, organized library delivery) is worth featuring as a case study. Included Health is a healthcare company -- different vertical entirely from construction. The relationship is likely corporate/enterprise referral.

6. NEON -- Proposal sent, not signed. More developed than first brief suggested.

NEON has a full dashboard with content ideas built out (same template structure as others). The dashboard infrastructure exists -- this wasn't just a proposal in a vacuum, AOM invested in building out the client experience. Whatever stalled it, the groundwork is done. Re-engaging NEON is a lighter lift than starting fresh.

7. Intelliplay -- Most distinctive proposal, highest-value stalled deal

The Intelliplay proposal is structurally different from the others: quarterly pricing ($9k Essentials, $15k Growth), includes a built-in podcast engine, and explicitly targets B2B lead generation rather than brand awareness. This is a tech company (FEC -- Family Entertainment Center technology). The podcast engine angle (record Zoom calls, AOM turns them into content suites) is smart and low-friction for the client. The content backlog includes "Direct Messaging Videos," "Meet the Team Videos," and "Location Opening January" -- this suggests Intelliplay had an upcoming location opening that may or may not have happened. The podcast idea is still in the backlog. Re-engaging here with a specific angle (the location opening + podcast launch package) could work.

The cost comparison table in their proposal is the most compelling sales document AOM has built. It frames the retainer against one-off shoot costs ($120k-$250k/year vs. $36k-$60k retainer). That math works for any B2B tech client doing event-based production.

8. PA-LA Restaurant -- Biggest creative scope, $3,500/month asking price

The PA-LA proposal is the most fully realized creative pitch in the dashboard. It's not a generic retainer template -- it's a named brand series ("The PA-LA Brand Series"), cinematic storytelling for a restaurant with two locations, scaling from 10 to 20 videos/month, plus a full amplification strategy section (paid ads, local TV, PR, radio). Asking price: $3,500/month. This is above the $3k target -- PA-LA would be the highest retainer on the books if it closes.

The proposal even includes a section on what AOM does NOT do (manage ad accounts directly) which shows maturity. This is a professional-grade proposal. Whatever stalled it is worth understanding.

9. NABI -- Template-heavy, relationship stalling

NABI's dashboard content is mostly unfilled template copy (placeholder posts like "Quick Tip: 3 Ways to Boost Your Productivity Today" with fake Dropbox links). The actual documentary relationship is the $25k NABI doc ("Letter to the World"). The social media retainer proposal appears to have been built out but the relationship is in a difficult place (client walking back funding). The gap between the template content and the real creative work tells the story: NABI was being set up for a retainer but hasn't converted.

10. Rafi Law Group -- Post-production only, not a retainer

Rafi is a completely different service model: post-production support for an existing show (6-8 episodes, Masterclass-style). AOM's role is post-production editor, not content strategist or social manager. Director/producer is Adrian McIntyre -- AOM is the hired post shop, not the creative lead. Three pricing tiers: $9,500 / $14,500 / $23,500 for 8 episodes. This is a significant one-off deal if it closes. Unknown status.

11. Skylar -- One project, one file

Skylar's dashboard has one item: "ALL I SEE IS YOU" music video. No additional detail visible beyond the file name. The relationship matters more for the ISA connection than for direct revenue.

12. Slick City Park -- Dead (confirmed)

Dashboard exists, proposal was sent (Essentials $2k/month, Growth $3.5k/month). Didn't close. The proposal is actually the same template that was accidentally used in LBX's folder -- which means LBX got sent a Slick City-branded proposal. That's worth checking: did LBX actually receive a correctly branded proposal?

What the Posts (Sample) CSV Reveals About AOM's Content Approach

The Posts (Sample) CSV is a template/demo file used to show clients what the Postiz-style scheduling system looks like. Three sample posts: install day reel, client story before/after, and "3 mistakes" educational content. All Instagram Reels. The hooks are tight: "Wait for the final reveal," "This changed everything for them," "If you're doing #2, stop." These are solid short-form hooks -- this is what AOM teaches clients to aim for.

Key takeaway: the content approach is Reels-first, hook-driven, short-form. The formula is: strong hook + visual payoff + action-oriented caption. This is the right approach for the construction vertical (contractors are increasingly active on Instagram/YouTube Shorts). The format works for every vertical in AOM's current book.

Pricing Reality Check (from actual proposals)

Client Model Rate
Ambition Mechanical Retainer $2k/month
KOHRS Retainer Unknown (Essentials tier = implied ~$2k)
LBX Retainer Unknown (same template)
Included Health One-off $9k
ISA Industries Multiple one-offs Unknown total, multiple deliverables
Intelliplay Quarterly retainer $9k-$15k/quarter ($3k-$5k/month equivalent)
PA-LA Restaurant Retainer (proposed) $3,500/month
Rafi Law Group Post-production $9,500-$23,500

The Intelliplay quarterly model is worth noting: billing quarterly instead of monthly could improve cash flow stability and reduce churn risk. If a client commits to a quarter upfront, they're less likely to cancel after month one.

Proposal Template Issue

Multiple proposals use identical Slick City / trampoline park language. LBX's proposal folder contains the Slick City template verbatim. This is a quality control issue in the sales process. If prospects are receiving proposals with wrong client names or wrong industry context, that undermines the "we understand your business" positioning that is central to AOM's pitch. Worth building a proposal QA step into the outreach workflow.

New Opportunities Surfaced by This Data

1. The ISA documentary series is AOM's biggest differentiator -- it needs to be visible. Episode 1 has a full production dashboard with a 12-18 minute story structure. Three intercut storylines. Real stakes (generator breakthrough, funding window, independent validation). This is the kind of work that wins awards and gets shared. When it's done, it needs to be the centerpiece of AOM's case study library. Nothing else in the portfolio is at this level of ambition.

2. The Intelliplay podcast engine concept is packageable as a standalone offer. "Record a Zoom call. We turn it into a full content suite." This is repeatable for any B2B company with a subject matter expert. It's low-friction for the client, high-value for AOM (editing, social clips, distribution). It doesn't require an on-site shoot. This could be a remote-first retainer offer -- meaningful for clients outside Phoenix.

3. Frame.io as the standard delivery workflow is a credibility signal worth highlighting. The Included Health SOW specifies Frame.io for all review and delivery with time-coded comments. That's a professional post-production workflow that positions AOM alongside agency-level operations. If this is the standard, it should be mentioned on the website and in all proposals.

4. KOHRS is potentially dormant -- worth a check-in. The dashboard shows December 2025 activity. It's now March 2026. No visible content past that date. If this retainer is still active, there should be more content. If it went quiet, that's a churn that happened without being logged. Jacob should verify status.

5. The LBX proposal branding error needs to be fixed before re-engaging. If LBX received a Slick City-branded proposal and signed anyway, that's fine. If they haven't signed, they may have received wrong-branded materials. Either way, if LBX is being re-engaged, send them a correctly branded document.

6. Rafi Law Group is a hidden high-value deal. $9,500 to $23,500 for post-production on a 6-8 episode series. This is a one-time deal but at the high end it's equivalent to 2+ months of a full retainer. Unknown status. Jacob should treat this as a priority check-in -- the post-production angle is different from AOM's usual pitch and requires less on-site production work.

What the First Brief Got Right

  • The Q1 gap analysis was accurate.
  • Ambition repricing to $3k is still the right move.
  • ISA/Skylar relationship management is real and important.
  • NEON, PA-LA, Intelliplay are the right re-engagement targets.
  • AI services teaser on the website is the right call.

What Changed or Got More Specific

  • Included Health is a one-off event shoot ($9k) not an ongoing retainer.
  • Intelliplay is a B2B tech company, not a construction/consumer company. Quarterly pricing model is different from monthly.
  • PA-LA is the highest proposed retainer ($3,500/month) -- if it closes, it exceeds the $3k target immediately.
  • Rafi Law Group is not a dead lead -- it's a post-production deal with real pricing. Should not have been in the "status unknown" pile.
  • KOHRS may be dormant since December 2025. Verify before assuming it's active.
  • LBX has a proposal branding error (Slick City template) -- low-level but worth fixing.

Biz Dev Brief -- 2026-03-07

What We Found

Revenue Reality Check

Q1 closes March 31. That's 24 days.

Confirmed active revenue:

  • Ambition Mechanical -- $2k/month retainer (social + filming). Website launched. Relationship is solid.
  • ISA Energy -- Brand video (one-off, $9k range). Hard deadline April 27. Work hasn't peaked yet.
  • Skylar -- Music video. One-off, in editing. No dollar figure in context files.
  • Brandon Wiley -- Documentary. One-off, in progress. No dollar figure in context files.
  • Included Health -- Retainer (details in Notion). Dollar figure unknown.
  • KOHRS -- Retainer (details in Notion). Dollar figure unknown.
  • LBX -- Documentary (details in Notion). Dollar figure unknown.

What we don't know (and need to know):

  • Exact monthly retainer amounts for KOHRS and Included Health
  • Current invoiced/collected totals for Q1 (Jan: ~$16k. Feb/Mar: ~$19k. Remaining gap unclear)
  • Where Skylar, Brandon Wiley, and LBX land on the revenue sheet -- are these invoiced now or on delivery?

The Q1 gap is real. The target is $50k. $16k in January, ~$19k projected for Feb/March. That implies the quarter ends around $35k unless something closes or gets invoiced before March 31. None of the open proposals (NEON, PA-LA, Intelliplay) are confirmed.

What's Actually Working vs. What's Planned

Working:

  • Corporate/brand video production. ISA Energy is proof. These close at ~$9k and have clear scope.
  • Website builds. Ambition Mechanical shipped. Stack is real (React + Tailwind + Firebase). Patrik can build.
  • Social media retainers. Ambition is the one paying model. $2k/month is under the $3k target -- this is a pricing problem, not a product problem.
  • The full-service pattern (website -> social -> filming). Ambition Mechanical is the case study. This is the model to replicate.

Planned but not yet real:

  • Construction vertical at scale (15 clients). One client is not a vertical.
  • AI auditing/agent services. Not on the website, not sold to anyone yet. The internal proof of concept is being built right now.
  • $3k/month retainer pricing. No client is currently paying that amount.
  • Postiz for scheduling. Not installed.
  • Apify for research. Not active.

Client Pattern Analysis

What closes:

  • Referral-adjacent relationships (ISA Energy came through the Skylar connection)
  • Clients who have a specific deliverable in mind (brand video, website, music video)
  • Companies with real budgets -- construction, energy, corporate

What stalls:

  • NABI -- Client walking back funding. This is a relationship management issue, not a sales issue.
  • Rafi Law Group -- Unknown status. No follow-up logged.
  • Slick City Park -- Dead.

Upsell pattern (proven once, worth scaling):

  • Website -> social media retainer -> on-site filming = full-service. Ambition Mechanical is the proof of concept.
  • Video production -> follow-on video work = ISA Energy pattern (Skylar's relationship creates more ISA work).

Undercharging:

  • Ambition Mechanical retainer at $2k vs. $3k target. That's a $1k/month gap on one client. If 15 clients close at $2k instead of $3k, that's $30k/month instead of $45k. Pricing discipline matters now.

Opportunities to Consider

1. Close the Q1 gap with existing clients before chasing new ones. The three open proposals (NEON, PA-LA, Intelliplay) are the fastest path to Q1 revenue. These are warm, not cold. Jacob should prioritize re-engaging all three before March 31. If even one signs at $9k, it materially closes the gap.

2. Raise Ambition Mechanical to $3k/month at the next renewal. The website is live, the retainer is running, the relationship is in good standing. This is the right moment to reposition the retainer value. Frame it around the full-service model now that the site is live: social + filming + ongoing web polish = $3k/month. A $1k bump on a happy client is the easiest revenue gain available.

3. Build one construction vertical case study before pitching anyone. The pitch to construction companies only works if there's a reference point. Ambition Mechanical is an HVAC/mechanical contractor -- that's construction-adjacent. Use it. Build out a social media case study (content calendar, post cadence, lead gen angle) while doing the work. That case study is the sales tool for the next 14 clients.

4. ISA Energy -> AOM relationship management. Skylar is a partner at ISA Energy. The music video and brand video are both AOM deliverables. Getting Skylar's video done before ISA workload peaks is a relationship investment, not just a task. Botching the Skylar video affects the ISA relationship. Nail both.

5. AI services -- not ready to sell publicly yet, but ready to pitch selectively. The internal system being built (agents, skills, context files) is real and working. It's not productized. It's not on the website. But it's far enough along to have a conversation with the right prospect -- specifically one who's already a client or close to becoming one. Do not launch this publicly yet. Do add it to the website as a teaser/waitlist signal. The product story (AOM is the proof of concept, skills as sellable modules) is compelling -- that framing belongs on the site now even if the product isn't fully packaged.

6. NABI revival -- bring in investors. The NABI doc ($25k planned) stalled because the client is walking back funding. Patrik's instinct to rally NABI + bring in investors is the right play if there's a genuine story worth telling. This is a longer path but the $25k payoff is real. Worth keeping alive. Jacob should probe whether NABI is still interested in the doc at all before pursuing the investor angle.

Website Changes to Make

The AOM-studio repo path is TBD (not confirmed locally). These are the changes needed -- Bobby should execute once the repo is located and Patrik approves direction.

  • Add AI services section. Not a full product page yet. A teaser section: what it is, who it's for, "working with select clients" framing with a contact/interest form. This plants the flag without overpromising.
  • Add AI auditing as a named service. Even if it's not fully packaged, naming it positions AOM ahead of the curve.
  • Skills as visual tiles. This is the long-term UI vision. Even a static version of this (6-8 tiles showing what the AI system can do) communicates the direction.
  • Remove or update anything that references old tagline / retired framing. "Excellence is the Baseline" is retired -- confirm it's gone everywhere.
  • Add a construction-specific case study or vertical callout. Once the Ambition case study is built, it goes on the site. Before that, even a construction-focused headline or industry callout signals to the vertical that AOM understands them.
  • Update services to reflect current offer stack. If AI auditing and agent services are planned additions, they should appear now in some form -- even as "coming soon" or waitlist.

Stalled Proposals Worth Re-Engaging

NEON -- re-engage now. Was promising. Proposal out, not signed. No context on what stalled it. Jacob should reach out with a check-in, not a hard close. Ask if scope or timing was the issue. If it was timing, now is the time -- Q2 is starting soon.

PA-LA Restaurant -- re-engage with a tighter offer. Restaurants are visual by nature. If the proposal included video and social, that's the right package. Jacob should lead with the visual storytelling angle and point to Ambition as proof of production quality. Keep the scope tight -- don't overwhelm them with options.

Intelliplay -- re-engage with a specific deliverable. No context on what the proposal included. Jacob should go back with a single clear offer (a brand video, a website, or a social package) rather than a full-service pitch. Easier to say yes to a specific thing.

Rafi Law Group -- status check. Unknown status. Was a proposal ever sent? Jacob should confirm and either follow up or mark it dead. Don't leave it in limbo.

NABI -- keep warm, don't push. Client is walking back funding. No point in a hard close right now. Jacob should maintain the relationship (check-in, no ask) and revisit in 60 days. The investor angle is worth exploring separately.

Questions for Patrik (RESOLVED 2026-03-09)

  • KOHRS, Included Health, LBX amounts? RESOLVED: Already in context/work.md. KOHRS $2k/month, Included Health $9k one-off, LBX $6k (on hold, behind on production). Alex should have read context files before asking.
  • AOM-studio repo location? RESOLVED: /Users/patrik/Documents/Dev/aom-studio. Already documented.
  • Ambition retainer renewal timing? RESOLVED: Already in context/work.md. Rate raises to $3.5k once consistent posting is established. Not a renewal -- it's a trigger-based increase.
  • Construction vertical pitch deck? RESOLVED: Check existing proposals in Notion archives (Ambition, KOHRS) for template/style reference. Build from those, not from scratch.
  • Why NEON, PA-LA, Intelliplay stalled? RESOLVED:
    • NEON: Patrik didn't finish pitching. Was overloaded. Pre-agent-team era.
    • PA-LA: Said they wanted to meet but Patrik was overloaded and didn't push hard.
    • Intelliplay: Beginning-of-year illness, then Patrik was pushing hard for new business mid-January and may have over-communicated with the PM.
  • AI services on the website? RESOLVED: Yes, ready to push forward on all fronts. Green light for teaser, waitlist, and website presence.
